c.tagline: Colonial charm, lakeside towers, and Indian Ocean sunsets in one tropical port city.

taxi.fareNote: Meters required by law for tuk-tuks and cabs but drivers often try to negotiate; use the PickMe or Uber app to lock in a fair metered fare.

avoid.reason: Pickpocketing in Pettah market and on buses; tuk-tuk overcharging — use meters/apps; gem scams

hood_desc: Colonial-era streets, the old port and gleaming new office towers make Fort the historic and business heart of the city; suits history buffs and business travelers wanting central sights within walking distance.

Colombo's beachfront promenade at Galle Face Green anchors this lively strip of malls, embassies, restaurants and nightlife; ideal for first-time visitors who want a central, walkable base with sunset ocean views.
A leafy, upscale residential district of museums, parks, embassies and boutique guesthouses; best for families and travelers who prefer quiet, green surroundings a short tuk-tuk ride from downtown.
A relaxed beach suburb south of the center with a long sandy beach, seafood shacks and a historic clifftop hotel; suits travelers wanting a beach base with an easy coastal train ride into the city.

A fast-redeveloping district around Beira Lake with new high-rise hotels and lakeside views, wedged between Fort and Galle Face; good for travelers wanting modern towers within easy walking distance of both.

water.note: Avoid tap water; stick to bottled or filtered water.

sys.n: Sri Lanka Railways (Coastal, Main & Puttalam Lines)

transit.pay: Train tickets are bought at station counters (season tickets and some e-ticketing available); city and intercity buses are paid in cash to the conductor with small rupee notes, and a citywide rechargeable transit card is not yet widespread.
transit.hours: Trains and buses generally run around 5am-10pm with sparse late-night service; after that, tuk-tuks, taxis or rideshare apps are the norm.
transit.note: Traffic congestion is heavy at peak hours; the Coastal Line train (Fort to Mount Lavinia/Galle) is a popular way to bypass road traffic along the southern suburbs.

tip.r: Not traditionally expected, but a 10% service charge is often added to hotel and restaurant bills; rounding up or a small extra tip for good service is appreciated, especially in tourist areas.
